historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Samriddhi was a goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. She was also known as Lakshmi in her role as the wife of Vishnu. Samriddhi is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Samriddhi was also the name of a king in ancient India, who ruled during the Mauryan Empire around the 3rd century BCE. He is known for his extensive trade networks and for promoting peaceful relations with neighboring kingdoms, contributing to the economic prosperity of his kingdom.
